elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.1: "Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a licence..."; 13.2 likewise grants the paid-up licence to "Customer and its Affiliates". Because "Customer" is defined as Meridian Fieldworks, Inc. alone, the express addition in 13.1 is the operative source of Affiliate coverage for the Services licence and is not duplicative of 13.2 (different subject matter: Services vs. paid-up software/Vendor Technology).

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.1 grants the licence to "contractors acting on Customer's behalf"; the prior exclusion "without Affiliates or contractors" is deleted. 13.2 separately permits contractors to support paid-up material.

Retained 13.2: "For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence..." Already met; no edit needed.

Retained 13.2 grants an "irrevocable" paid-up licence, and 13.3 confirms Vendor "shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach... after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure."

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.1 replaces "revocable at Vendor's sole discretion" with a licence "revocable only for Customer's uncured material breach", tracking the standard already in 13.3 (notice and cure opportunity). No at-will revocation right remains for the Services (subscription) licence.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Retained 13.3: "Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24." The redline's deletion of "non-transferable" from 13.1 removes the contradictory retained sentence that would otherwise defeat this right for the Services licence.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.1 covers Affiliates unconditionally, which exceeds the fallback's notice-conditioned coverage; the written-notice condition is unnecessary because no notice trigger gates the grant.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: 13.3 permits transfer to "an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24"; the conflicting "non-transferable" wording in 13.1 has been removed so the successor-transfer right is operative for the Services licence as well.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met on the operative language: 13.1 as rewritten supplies Affiliate and contractor coverage and the uncured-material-breach-only revocation standard, while retained 13.2 (perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid) and 13.3 (transfer to Affiliate or successor) already carried the remaining elements. The position is complete at the preferred level, so the fallback is not needed.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to 13.1 and touches only words that block a selected element — "alone" and "without Affiliates or contractors" (Affiliate/contractor elements), "revocable at Vendor's sole discretion" (subscription-revocation element), and "non-transferable" (successor-transfer element, which would otherwise contradict retained 13.3). No survival tail, expense language, notice procedure, or other boilerplate was added.

No duplication: "Customer" is defined as Meridian Fieldworks, Inc. alone, so Affiliates were not already inside the defined term, and 13.2's Affiliate grant covers only paid-up software/Vendor Technology, not the Services licence in 13.1. The separate contractor reference in 13.1 is needed because 13.2's contractor permission is limited to paid-up material.

Intent is preserved: 13.2 and 13.3 survive unchanged, the new revocation standard mirrors 13.3 rather than contradicting it, the Section 24 cross-reference remains intact, and no defined term is left dangling.

Residual point for the drafter (rationale note only, not a defect): the successor-transfer right in 13.3 runs through "an assignment permitted by Section 24", so its scope depends on Section 24's M&A permission; if Section 24 later narrows, the transfer element would need a direct successor carve-out in 13.3.
